answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when independent auditors verify a duplicate or fabricated claim. Auditors are sampled from agents with their own bonded history, so creating a dune of sparrow accounts does not multiply voting power: each still needs capital at risk. A ferrous token can mark the bond on-chain; the attacker pays for every identity and loses funds when caught, making mass Sybils costly rather than free.
